tasks.prompt: Compute the ISO 8601 week number and ISO week-year for each date: 2024-12-30, 2021-01-03, 2026-01-01, 2020-12-31. Return answer as an array of objects with keys "date", "week" (integer) and "year" (integer), in the given order.

Sort these records by dept ascending, then score descending, then age ascending, then name ascending: [{"name": "ivy", "dept": "ops", "age": 31, "score": 88}, {"name": "abe", "dept": "eng", "age": 45, "score": 92}, {"name": "kai", "dept": "eng", "age": 31, "score": 92}, {"name": "bo", "dept": "ops", "age": 27, "score": 75}, {"name": "cy", "dept": "eng", "age": 27, "score": 81}, {"name": "dee", "dept": "hr", "age": 31, "score": 88}]. Return answer as the array of names in sorted order.

Merge overlapping or touching closed intervals [[8,10],[1,3],[2,6],[15,18],[10,12],[17,20],[6,7]] (intervals that share an endpoint merge). Return answer as the sorted array of merged [start, end] pairs.

Edges mean the first task must run before the second: [["lint", "test"], ["build", "test"], ["fetch", "build"], ["fetch", "lint"], ["test", "deploy"], ["docs", "deploy"]]. Return answer as a topological order of all tasks, always choosing the alphabetically smallest available task next.
Count business days (Monday to Friday) strictly after 2026-12-18 up to and including 2027-01-08, excluding holidays 2026-12-25 and 2027-01-01. Return answer as an integer.
Base64-encode the UTF-8 string "Nisi: café ☕" using standard padding. Return answer as the encoded string.

Compute the Levenshtein edit distance (insert, delete, substitute, each cost 1) for each pair: ["kitten","sitting"], ["flaw","lawn"], ["intention","execution"], ["abc",""]. Return answer as an array of integers in the given order.
Run-length encode "aaabccddddde" as count followed by character for every run, including runs of length 1. Return answer as the encoded string.
Evaluate 7 - 3 * (2 + 4) / 6 + 2 ** 3 ** 2 / 64 where ** is exponentiation (right-associative, higher precedence than * and /). Return answer as a number.

Sum amount by region for [{"region": "north", "amount": 12.345}, {"region": "south", "amount": 7.125}, {"region": "north", "amount": 3.335}, {"region": "east", "amount": 0.005}, {"region": "south", "amount": 2.5}], then round each sum to 2 decimals using round-half-to-even on the exact decimal value. Return answer as an object mapping region to the rounded sum, with keys in alphabetical order.

Normalize each phone number to E.164, assuming US (+1) when there is no country code and dropping extensions; a number that cannot be normalized becomes null. Numbers: ["(415) 555-0132", "+44 20 7946 0958", "415.555.0199 x12", "001 212 555 0100", "555-0100"]. A leading 001 is the international prefix for +1. Return answer as an array in the given order.

In the text "The quick brown fox, the lazy dog; THE end. A fox! Then the fox ran.", lowercase every word and strip the punctuation characters . , ; ! from word ends. Return answer as an array of the 3 most frequent words as [word, count] pairs, ordered by count descending then word ascending.
Convert MCMXCIV and MMXXIV to integers, add them, and return answer as the sum written in Roman numerals.
Add 3/8, 5/12 and 7/18 exactly and return answer as an object {"numerator": n, "denominator": d} in lowest terms.
For each date give the English weekday name: 1969-07-20, 2000-02-29, 2038-01-19, 1900-03-01. Return answer as an array of strings in the given order.

Sort these versions by Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 precedence, lowest first: ["1.0.0","1.0.0-rc.1","1.0.0-alpha","1.0.0-alpha.1","1.0.0-beta.11","1.0.0-beta.2","1.0.0-alpha.beta","1.0.0-beta"]. Return answer as the sorted array.
